findings.finding: Q3 credit is running ahead of the company's own Q3 guide. Monthly 8-Ks show a net principal loss rate of 6.80% in July and 6.40% in August, against 7.63% and 7.57% a year earlier, so Jul-Aug averages about 6.6% against the guided ~6.68% (Q2 6.98% less 30bp). Delinquency was 5.36% at August, against 5.84% a year earlier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the NLR beat its trajectory (6.98%, -90bp y/y) and EPS of $3.55 beat $2.68, yet the stock moved +1.68% and slipped about 1% in the following days (https://www.webull.com/news/15312903333815296). Q1 2026: EPS $4.18 against $3.04, move -0.35%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the monthly 8-Ks are public and in the wire. Only September's number is unknown; BFH does not file it monthly before the print (no October 8-K on EDGAR). If the Q3 beat were unpriced, consensus would not already sit below Q2 actuals. It does ($3.38 against $3.55), so the street models seasonality, not credit.
findings.independence: July 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1101215/000110121526000076/july2026creditstatsex991-t.htm) is the same company series. Peer Synchrony's Q3 NCO of 4.79%, -37bp y/y (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001601712/000160171226000040/earningsrelease3q26.htm), points the same way.

findings.finding: The FY2026 net loss rate guide of 7.0-7.1% looks conservative. With Q1 at 7.33%, Q2 at 6.98% and Q3 tracking about 6.6%, it implies a Q4 of roughly 7.1-7.5%. Q4 2025 was 7.4%, so the guide implies -30bp to +10bp y/y in Q4, against -83bp to -117bp y/y in July-August. Another cut to the NLR guide, to about 6.9-7.0%, is the arithmetic outcome unless management sees Q4 deterioration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The NLR guide was improved from 7.2-7.4% to 7.0-7.1% at Q2 and the stock moved +1.68%. The first 2026 guide in Jan 2026 moved it +7.08%, and Oct 2025 moved it +8.13%. Guidance prints have produced the large moves; reported-quarter beats have not.
findings.why_not_priced: A partially priced inference. The street has seen two consecutive guide improvements and the run-up suggests it expects a third. If a deeper cut were fully priced, the stock would already trade above every published target (avg about $108-111) rather than at it. Q4 2025's 7.4% comes from the Jan 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1101215/000110121526000007/exhibit991epr01-29x26.htm); the y/y comparison is my arithmetic, not a published figure.
findings.independence: Shares the monthly-8-K input with finding 1, but lands on a different line (the forward guide, not the quarter). Synchrony on 2026-10-20 reported NCO -37bp y/y and described credit as 'strong' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001601712/000160171226000040/earningsrelease3q26.htm). It also built $30M of reserve, a hint that issuers are not extrapolating credit gains.

findings.finding: Loan growth is accelerating past the guide's midpoint. Average loans grew 2.9% y/y in Q2, 4.1% in June, 4.9% in July and 5.6% in August (end of period $18.73B against $17.66B). The FY guide is 'low- to mid-single digits' for average loans and revenue, so Q3 revenue should be near +5% against a consensus of about $1.01B, and the loan/revenue guide could move to 'mid-single digits'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At Q2 the loan and revenue guide was raised from 'low single digits' to 'low- to mid-single digits' alongside the NLR improvement, for +1.68% on the day. The market's open worry after Q2 was 'modest loan growth' and lower non-interest income (https://www.webull.com/news/15312903333815296).
findings.why_not_priced: The monthly loan balances are public, but revenue consensus of about $1.01B implies only about +4% y/y, below the 5%+ average-loan growth the 8-Ks show for July-August. If the acceleration were priced into revenue, consensus would sit nearer $1.02-1.03B. Growth also forces a reserve build (CECL on a larger book), which caps the EPS effect.
findings.independence: June and July credit-stat 8-Ks (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001101215/000110121526000069/june2026creditstatsex991-t.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1101215/000110121526000076/july2026creditstatsex991-t.htm). Synchrony Q3 purchase volume +8% and loans +3% (peer read, same week).

findings.finding: Management guided expenses up sequentially in Q3 and Q4. It also said NIM may dip seasonally in Q3 ('a slight Q3 decline would be acceptable'), and that buybacks would slow in Q3 (about $25M in July against $241M in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: These were the post-Q2 complaints (higher expense guide, lower late-fee and non-interest income), and the stock drifted about 1% lower in the week after a big beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is inside the company's guide, and consensus ($3.38) is already below Q2's $3.55. It is filed because an expense or NIM overshoot is the one way a credit beat turns into a 'quality of beat' sell.
findings.independence: Synchrony Q3 NIM -12bp y/y to 15.50% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001601712/000160171226000040/earningsrelease3q26.htm), the same direction on NIM.

findings.finding: Closest peer Synchrony reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-20: EPS $2.68 against about $2.42 consensus, NCO 4.79% (-37bp y/y), 30+ delinquency 4.34% (-5bp), purchase volume +8%, NIM -12bp, $30M reserve build. This is a clean private-label-card read-through after BFH last spoke.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measured for BFH on peer days. BFH's +8.8% 5-day run-up spans Synchrony's print, which suggests the read-through has already been taken.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: BFH rose about 8.8% over the five sessions that include Synchrony's print, and +3.25% on 10-21. Kept small because Synchrony's delinquency improvement narrowed to -5bp y/y. BFH's own August delinquency was still -48bp y/y, so the peer is not a direct template.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers SYF consensus $2.42 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/syf); BFH's own monthly 8-Ks (finding 1).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: +8.8% in 5 days and +8.55% in 20, within 5% of the 52-week high, at or above the average target of about $108-111. Short interest is rising: 2.79M at 09-15, 3.24M (8.4% of shares, DTC 4.8) at 09-30. Skew is flat at +1.0 vol points.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the stock went in near $107-108 and a large beat produced +1.68% and then drifted lower. The bar implied by the run-up is now a guide improvement, not a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The run-up raises the bar for a sell-the-news move. Moderate, rising short interest partially offsets it, being squeeze fuel if the guide improves, so the finding is sized small.

findings.finding: Capital return and financing: management said the next preferred issuance would come 'no sooner than Q4 2026' and that the buyback pace slows while loan growth absorbs capital. $449M remained on the authorization at Q2, and CET1 was 12.9%. The call may announce a preferred deal and say how buybacks resume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The May 2026 Series B preferred (8.875%) was flagged as a cost-of-capital concern after Q2 (https://www.webull.com/news/15312903333815296). There is no isolated reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: it funds loan growth the 8-Ks show is real (+5.6% y/y in August), so it is not distress. It is near zero, slightly negative only because slower buybacks remove EPS support.

findings.finding: Revolver Amendment No. 2 (2026-09-03, JPMorgan agent, $700M facility) permits the merger of Comenity Bank into Comenity Capital Bank. Regulators approved it on 2026-07-31 and it was expected to close around 2026-10-01. The company says it is not expected to significantly affect financial position, results or liquidity. Q3/Q4 may carry one-off merger costs or funding simplification.
findings.why_not_priced: A covenant waiver for an internal bank merger is not distress. It is sized at zero because the company says it is immaterial; filed for completeness.

findings.finding: Leadership change: Chief Commercial Officer Valerie Greer retires around 2027-02-19 (retirement agreement, $945k cash). Dennis McCarthy became EVP and Chief Revenue Officer in early September 2026. All top-10 partner programs are renewed to at least 2028 per the company, and no partner loss was found in 2026 news.
findings.why_not_priced: Old news. Filed because the sweep asked about partner wins and losses: the answer is no loss found, and new 2026 programs (Ford in March, Academy Sports in March) support the loan acceleration in finding 3.

findings.finding: The reserve rate has room to fall. Q2's allowance was 11.23% of loans, and management said the CECL rate 'will get down around that 10% target' as credit improves. With NLR down about 100bp y/y, Q3 can absorb the growth-driven build and still release rate, which favours another EPS beat against $3.38. BFH has beaten EPS by more than $0.80 in each of Q1 and Q2 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat $4.18 against $3.04 for -0.35%; Q2 2026 beat $3.55 against $2.68 for +1.68%. Reserve-driven EPS beats have not been paid for.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts have under-modelled reserve releases two quarters running: consensus was 27-37% light. This suggests the line is not modelled, but the stock does not pay for it, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Benzinga history of Q1/Q2 actual against estimate (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BFH/earnings-forecasts). Synchrony built reserve in Q3 ($30M), which points the other way for the industry.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive, on a guide that looks conservative and accelerating loans, which agrees with the flat skew. They cut against the +8.8% five-day run-up, which already prices a good peer read-through, and against this name's habit of not paying for EPS beats; so p_up is held at 56.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): shrank the two reported-quarter findings that BFH has not paid for, the Q3 NLR from +0.4 to +0.2 and the reserve-driven beat from +0.5 to +0.3, citing Q1/Q2 2026 beats of 30%+ for -0.35% and +1.68%.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked at 8.4% of shares outstanding, DTC 4.8, rising. Moderate, not crowded, but the rise is squeeze fuel, so the run-up negative was shrunk from -0.8 to -0.6.
Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 5.5 to 6.0, since guidance quarters on this name moved 7-8%.

Rule 2, 4 and 6 checks left the rest standing: guidance findings kept at full size; the bar is sourced to two agreeing estimates plus the company's Q3 NLR guide; financing was signed after asking what it funds (loan growth); every finding resolves 2026-10-22.
